pairs.subject: paged-block-cache
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/cache.rs:68 The cache key is one SHA-256 over a whole request (method, url, body, sorted headers, proxy), so each request produces one key for one whole stored response; there is no prefix-monotone computation, no fixed-size block or block pool, and no chained per-block key. Searching crates/core for parent_key, block_hash, prefix_cache, block_size and free_list found 0 hits, so the subject's precondition does not hold here.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/cache.rs:72 Whole-artifact content key over unordered request attributes, not blocks of an ordered input. The technique's 'unordered inputs' exclusion applies: plain content addressing is correct here.

crates/core/src/cache.rs:288 No per-request append-only reference table exists. Entries are long-lived SQLite rows upserted in place, which is the technique's own 'long-lived/mutable entries' exclusion.

crates/core/src/cache.rs:344 Entries are independent whole responses with no parent/descendant structure, so the releasing party has no depth signal. Oldest-confirmed eviction is the fallback the technique itself names.
crates/core/src/lru.rs:21 No fixed-page memory pool shared by consumer classes with different per-element costs. The LRU caps a count of keyed handles, not paged memory.
